newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua port operators say strike still expected.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua port operators say strike still expected.

text.p: Port operators at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua said they had still not struck a deal with dock workers over a pay dispute and there was a 90 percent chance that a strike would go ahead on March 5.
"It has not been solved, the chance of a strike is 90 percent," said Ana Lucia Ferrera, chief negotiator for the port operators union SINDOP.
A spokesman for the dock workers union confirmed that they still had not received a reply from the port operators to a proposal to call off the strike in exchange for an immediate pay rise.
However he was optimistic a solution would be reached by Tuesday evening.
"Everything indicates there will not be a strike," he said.
They are demanding a 21 percent wage increase which they say they are owed since last year.
Directors of SINDOP were still meeting to discuss their response to the dock workers proposal, Ferrera said

A general assembly of all Paranagua port operators was scheduled to be held at 1700 local (2000 GMT). The dock workers spokesman said he was hopeful a solution could be reached shortly after that meeting.
